Test a partition of the tree against random partitions

Source: R/damocles_configurations.R
damocles_partition_test.Rd

damocles_partition_test() asks whether rates that change among regimes fit the local presences better than rates that change among partitions of the same complexity placed at random on the tree (random_regimes()). The statistic is the likelihood ratio of the fit with regimes against constant rates, with parameters shared by all communities (damocles_lrt()); its p-value is the proportion of random partitions with a statistic as large or larger.

Usage

damocles_partition_test(
  comm,
  tree,
  regimes,
  n_rand = 99,
  vary = c("both", "gamma", "mu"),
  root = c("both", "absent", "present"),
  sympatry = 0,
  tolerance = 2,
  max_overlap = 0.25,
  cores = 1
)

Arguments

comm

Presences of the species (columns, named as the tips of tree) in one or more communities (rows): a matrix or data frame, or a named vector for one community. Values above zero count as presences. Tips missing from comm count as absent, with a warning, and species of comm missing from the tree are dropped.

tree

A rooted, fully dichotomous phylo tree with branch lengths.

regimes

Regime of each edge of tree, in the order of tree$edge, with two or more regimes.

n_rand

Number of random partitions drawn; each distinct one is fitted once.

vary

Which rates change among regimes or with edge_covariate: "both", "gamma" or "mu"; the other one is a single rate for the whole tree.

root

Prior on the state of the ancestor at the root: "both", "absent" or "present".

sympatry

In damocles_loglik(), the probability that a present ancestor leaves both daughters present (see simulate_damocles()). In damocles_fit(), a fixed value, or NULL to estimate it with the rates (shared or not, as they are).

tolerance, max_overlap

Passed to random_regimes(): random clades hold between 1 / tolerance and tolerance times as many edges as the clades of regimes, share at most max_overlap of their edges with them (Jaccard index), and the whole random partition agrees with regimes at most as much (adjusted Rand index).

cores

Number of cores, with random partitions fitted in parallel. Not available on Windows, where one core is used. The random partitions are drawn before the fits, so the p-value does not depend on the number of cores.

Value

A list of class mc_damocles_partition with the observed statistic, its degrees of freedom df, the chi-squared p-value p_chisq, the p-value against random partitions p_random (NA when no random partition could be drawn), the statistics of the distinct random partitions null, their number n_distinct, and fit, the fit with regimes.

Details

The chi-squared test of damocles_lrt() asks whether rates vary at all along the tree in the way the partition allows. When they vary somewhere, any partition captures part of that and the chi-squared test rejects constant rates even for a partition unrelated to where the rates change. The random partitions keep the number of parameters and the sizes of the clades, so this test asks instead whether the partition given is better placed than arbitrary ones: whether the regimes from a method of diversification, or a partition defined a priori, carry information on local colonisation and extinction beyond rate heterogeneity in general. data-raw/validation_damocles.R shows the difference between the two tests: with 40 replicates of 10 communities on trees of 60 tips and a clade holding about a quarter of the edges, the chi-squared test rejected constant rates in 3 of 40 without an effect, in 40 of 40 with colonisation faster in the clade, and in 29 of 40 with it faster in another clade of similar size; the test against random partitions rejected in 4, 37 and 0 of 40. The 4 of 40 without an effect is within sampling error of 5% but may be slightly liberal.

Random partitions that nearly coincide with the one tested, such as the clade one edge above it, capture the same rates and leave the test without power: with max_overlap = 1 the test against random partitions rejected in none of 40 replicates with the effect in the clade. The default max_overlap = 0.25 keeps only placements elsewhere on the tree, so the test asks whether the partition beats partitions of the same complexity placed somewhere else. With the whales and the best BAMM configuration of BAMMtools (a regime on 69 of 172 edges) and colonisation three times faster in it, both tests rejected constant rates (p = 0.007 and 0.01; data-raw/damocles_bamm.R).

The test needs room on the tree for clades like those of regimes elsewhere. When the partition tested is one of the clades at the root, or a clade holding most of the tree, the only placements allowed may split the tree as regimes does (its complement) or be few, and the random statistics then repeat a handful of values: the p-value falls at its smallest or at one depending on numerical noise. In simulations with one shift in the rate of speciation and no effect on local rates (data-raw/s1_type1_shifts.R), this made the test reject in 12% to 40% of replicates before random partitions matching regimes were excluded (random_regimes()) and before the p-value counted each distinct partition once. The n_rand draws are a way to find distinct placements: the p-value is the proportion of the distinct random partitions, plus the one tested, with a statistic as large or larger, so with fewer than 19 distinct ones it cannot fall below 0.05 (a warning says so). Trees with a strong shift in diversification often leave that little room; then only the chi-squared test of damocles_lrt() is available.

See also

random_regimes(), damocles_samples(), damocles_lrt().

Examples

set.seed(9)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(30)
reg <- clade_regimes(tr, list(A = ape::Ntip(tr) + 2))
comm <- simulate_damocles(tr, ifelse(reg == "A", 3, 0.5), mu = 1, n = 5)
damocles_partition_test(comm, tr, reg, n_rand = 19, vary = "gamma")
#> Warning: only 18 distinct random partitions in 19 draws: the tree has few places for clades like those of `regimes`, and `p_random` cannot be below 0.053
#> Partition of the tree against 18 random partitions (DAMOCLES)
#> Likelihood ratio against constant rates: 28.07 on 1 df
#> p (chi-squared): 1.17e-07 
#> p (random partitions): 0.0526 (18 distinct random partitions)
